title: Governor configuration (version 1)
description: The §8 versioned config contract, hand-written against the actual Deserialize/validate() behavior of Config and its nested types in src/config.rs, and checked against every real fixture under examples/*.yaml. version is pinned to the literal 1 because Config::validate() rejects anything else outright ('unsupported config version'); a future version 2 gets its own schema file rather than a union here, matching the plan's 'new top-level version' compatibility rule. Every object here mirrors a #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] struct, so additionalProperties is false throughout (unlike quota-snapshot.schema.json, which mirrors permissive structs). One class of Config::validate() rule is documented but NOT enforced by this schema, because vanilla JSON Schema has no portable way to express it: cross-field numeric comparisons on sibling properties -- max_workers >= min_workers, bootstrap_workers <= max_workers, host max_workers <= the account's max_workers -- there is no standard keyword to compare two named properties against each other. §8's 'Poll, staleness, sample, and transport durations are positive and bounded' IS enforced (validate_duration() in src/config.rs, subgov-634ba279): every duration field below has minimum 1 and maximum i64::MAX, the same overflow-guard bound already used for banked_resets.deadline_safety_seconds. Where JSON Schema can express a Config::validate() rule (target/reserve exclusivity and ranges, non-empty argv, the {desired_workers} placeholder, non-empty accounts map), it does.

version.description: Config::validate() requires this to equal 1 exactly.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX.

state_path.description: A leading ~/ is expanded; no other shell/environment expansion runs.

accounts.description: At least one account is required. Keys are account names; non-emptiness and uniqueness of keys are guaranteed by object/mapping syntax itself.

argv.description: validate_argv(): non-empty array, no empty element. Never interpreted by a shell (§7.4).

source.description: SourceConfig -- internally tagged on `type`, rename_all snake_case, deny_unknown_fields per variant.

timeout_seconds.description: Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX.
Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX.
Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX.

agent.description: NEEDLE adapter name; Config::validate() permits ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'.

heartbeat_dir.description: NEEDLE heartbeat directory; a leading ~/ is expanded.

stale_after_seconds.description: Ignore heartbeats older than this many seconds. Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX.

actuator.description: ActuatorConfig -- internally tagged on `type`, defaults to {"type": "none"} when the account omits `actuator` entirely (schema-level default only; this schema validates the document as written, it does not itself substitute the default into a missing key).

allOf.description: validate_fleet() requires an actuator command to contain {desired_workers} in at least one argument; source and observer commands do not have this requirement.

adapter.description: NEEDLE agent adapter. Its `needle-<adapter>-*` tmux session namespace is the pool managed by this actuator.

fleet.description: max_workers >= min_workers and bootstrap_workers <= max_workers are enforced by Config::validate() but not expressible here -- see the top-level description. `observer` is required unless `hosts` is configured, and `observer`/a non-none `actuator` are mutually exclusive with `hosts` (plan.md §22.2/§22.3); validate_fleet()/validate_host() enforce both, not expressible here.

hosts.description: plan.md §22.2/§22.3: optional and additive. When present, at least one host is required (validate_fleet()); when absent, the account behaves byte-identically to v0.1 via `observer`/`actuator` above.

host.description: HostConfig (plan.md §22.3). max_workers <= the account's fleet.max_workers, and resource_reserve is required whenever resource_source is set, both enforced by validate_host() and not expressible here.

resourceReserve.description: plan.md §22.3/§22.8: neither field has a safe default, so both are required whenever a host declares resource_reserve at all.

resourceSource.description: ResourceSourceConfig -- internally tagged on `type`, reusing the generic file/http/command transport from §7.4 verbatim (§22.5).

timeout_seconds.description: Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX.

utilization.description: validate_target(..., required=true): exactly one of target_utilization/reserve_fraction is required at account level.

stale_after_seconds.description: Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX. A deliberately huge value (e.g. 315360000, 10 years) is a valid way to effectively disable staleness -- see examples/all-three.yaml.

minimum_sample_seconds.description: Config::validate() rejects 0 or a value above i64::MAX.

windowPolicy.description: validate_target(..., required=false): a window override may set at most one of target_utilization/reserve_fraction, and either or both may be entirely absent (inherits the account-level policy).

bankedResets.description: Policy for earned, one-shot quota resets (e.g. Codex banked resets). Every field has a Rust-side default, so none are required.

deadline_safety_seconds.description: Config::validate() rejects a value above i64::MAX.
